dimension: Dead weight and structural duplication across the whole repo
summary: The repo carries roughly 2,300 lines of source that nothing can reach — 11 unreachable API routes, 3 unusable email-provider adapters, ~512 lines of never-called email functions, an entire table-partitioning subsystem for a schema shape that does not exist in production, and 7 orphaned components/templates — plus 11 database tables with zero rows AND zero code references. But the expensive dead weight is not the code; it is machinery that runs. `retryFailedEmails()` (lib/services/scheduler.service.ts:72) is a self-amplifying loop that has written 44,969 email_logs rows for a single already-verified group, still grows ~1,030/day, and consumes ~100% of the daily email quota — 194 of the 196 emails "sent" on 2026-09-04 were this one loop. Two more job types have executed 12,025 times against tables that have never held a single row. Meanwhile the migration ledger has diverged badly: 37 shipped migration files (4,419 lines of SQL) are applied to production but absent from `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, and 2 more are applied by CI but never by production — so CI's `journal_lines` is a partitioned table while production's is a plain 66-row table. Four churn tables now account for 89.1% of the public schema against 9 groups and 4 loans.

findings.title: retryFailedEmails() is a self-amplifying loop: 44,969 log rows and ~100% of the daily email quota burned re-sending one verification email to one already-verified group
findings.evidence:
lib/services/scheduler.service.ts:72-104 — selects up to 50 `email_logs` rows WHERE status='failed' AND created_at >= NOW()-'24 hours', then calls sendTemplatedEmail() for each. sendTemplatedEmail→sendEmailWithFallback→adapter INSERTs a BRAND-NEW email_logs row per provider attempt (lib/email/adapters/resend.ts:21, lib/email/adapters/smtp.ts:30). There is no attempt counter, no cap, and the original row is never marked retried — so every retry manufactures ≥1 new retry-eligible failed row. It also passes `vars: {}` (line 92), so even a successful retry sends a template with no variables filled.
Live prod: `SELECT template_key, status, count(*), count(DISTINCT "to") FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1,2` → group_verification_link: 40,733 failed / 3,629 queued / 609 sent, ALL to 1 distinct address. `SELECT el.group_id, g.name, g.status, count(*) FROM email_logs el LEFT JOIN groups g ON g.id=el.group_id WHERE template_key='group_verification_link' GROUP BY 1,2,3` → 44,969 rows for "Munyali Ukulima Self Help Group", whose group_status is already **active** — the verification it keeps re-sending completed long ago. First row 2026-08-16, still running: `SELECT created_at::date, count(*) ... GROUP BY 1` → 1,056/1,052/1,036/1,036/1,018/1,006 rows per day for the last week.
Timing proof it is the retry job and not a user: rows land at exactly :00/:05/:10… past the hour, in the same tick as the cron. `SELECT l.created_at, q.type, l.status, l.message FROM job_logs l JOIN job_queue q ON q.id=l.job_id WHERE l.created_at BETWEEN '2026-09-05 00:44' AND '2026-09-05 00:51'` → email_retry_failed logs "Starting" at 00:45:15 and 00:50:12 and NEVER logs a completion; the four email_logs rows for that tick land at 00:45:16, :17, :48, :49. The job is last in the tick and the 50 s batch budget kills it mid-run every time — which is exactly why the lead's banked "email_retry_failed last success 2026-08-20" is true.
findings.impact: Consumes the entire provider quota every day, so the email outage the user "fixed" on 2026-09-03 is re-broken daily: `SELECT created_at::date, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status='sent') ... GROUP BY 1` → 2026-09-04 sent=196 of which 194 were group_verification_link, failed=782 ("You have reached your daily email sending quota"); 2026-09-03 sent=200 of which 200 were this loop. staff_operational_alert, account_statement and weekly_summary all fail for want of quota. Adds ~1,030 rows/day to email_logs (now 46,270 rows / 22 MB, 97.2% of it this one loop) and burns 2,063,727 ms of job compute across 4,200 logged runs.
findings.recommendation: Add an attempt counter (or a `retry_count`/`last_retry_at` column) and a hard cap to email_logs, and make retryFailedEmails() UPDATE the existing row rather than INSERT a new one via the full send pipeline; exclude a template whose underlying flow has completed (group.status <> 'pending_verification'). Immediately: stop enqueueing email_retry_failed until capped, and delete/park the 44,969 group_verification_link rows so the 24 h retry window drains. Also fix the `vars: {}` bug — a retry currently cannot produce a usable email even when it succeeds.

findings.title: 37 shipped migrations (4,419 lines of SQL) are applied to production but absent from the migration tracking table, and 2 more are applied by CI but never by production
findings.evidence:
`SELECT count(*) FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` → 152 tracked names; `supabase/migrations/` holds 189 files. Diffing names: 38 files are untracked, of which 169 is the unshipped one on this branch — so 37 shipped migrations are untracked, totalling 4,419 lines. The set is 094, 095, 109-118, 123-134, 147-151, 159-166 (the lead's known 147-151 case is 5 of 37). Verified applied-but-untracked by object existence, not assumption: to_regclass('public.sms_provider_health_state') IS NOT NULL (163), staff_alert_state exists (165), sms_opt_outs exists (162), private.assign_allocation_code exists (117), idx_funding_programs_repayable exists (116), idx_org_disb_repayable exists (117), organizations.logo_url exists (109).
Two were never applied to prod at all: `SELECT (SELECT relkind FROM pg_class WHERE oid=to_regclass('public.journal_lines')), to_regclass('public.journal_lines_partitioned') IS NOT NULL, to_regclass('public.journal_lines_legacy') IS NOT NULL` → 'r', false, false — 094/095 (201 lines) never ran.
CI runs every file regardless: .github/workflows/ci.yml:429-437 `for f in $(ls supabase/migrations/*.sql | sort); do psql ... -f "$f"; done`. So CI's journal_lines is a PARTITIONED table with a journal_lines_legacy sibling; production's is a plain table with 66 rows.
One more mismatch: the tracking table holds the name `fix_audit_logs_insert_policy` while the repo file is `114_fix_audit_logs_insert_policy.sql`, so that migration will re-run too. Control: the reverse check found no drift — only 2 of 144 prod tables have no CREATE TABLE in the migration set, and both (organizations, organization_group_access) are explained by the 050 rename migration.
findings.impact: Any CLI-driven deploy (`supabase db push`) or a rebuild from the ledger would attempt to re-run 37 migrations against a schema that already has their effects — many contain non-idempotent DDL (e.g. 116 does `ALTER TABLE organization_ledger DROP CONSTRAINT organization_ledger_entry_type_check` with no IF EXISTS). Independently, every integration test that touches journal_lines validates behaviour against a partitioned schema shape that does not exist in production, so the accounting suite proves nothing about the live table.
findings.recommendation: Backfill the 37 missing rows into supabase_migrations.schema_migrations using the same version/name convention scripts/ops/apply-migration.ts:20-31 derives, and rename the `fix_audit_logs_insert_policy` row to `114_fix_audit_logs_insert_policy`. Then decide 094/095: either apply them to production or delete both files — leaving them applied only in CI keeps the accounting test suite testing a fiction.

findings.title: Time-bucketed dedup keys mint a job row every 5 minutes whether or not there is work — the fix was applied to the 4 SMS sweeps only, and the code says so explicitly
findings.evidence:
lib/jobs/index.ts:62-79 — email_campaign_process, email_retry_failed and email_campaign_drain each use `dedup_key: '<type>:${dateStr}T${hour}:${fiveMinBucket}'`. The comment block at lib/jobs/index.ts:81-108 diagnoses this exact defect for the SMS sweeps ("it minted a NEW row every 5 minutes whether or not the previous one had ever run… the backlog then became its own cause"), fixes those four with a CONSTANT dedup key, and then states: "Deliberately NOT applied to the mpesa_*/outbox_* sweeps in the same file: they have the same shape and probably want the same treatment, but they were not part of the SMS audit and are not changed blind."
Production consequence, `SELECT type, status, count(*), min(created_at), max(created_at) FROM job_queue WHERE type IN (...) GROUP BY 1,2`: the six types still on time-bucketed keys hold 3,702 + 3,652 + 4,613 + 2,849 + 2,488 + 2,159 = 19,463 pending rows, with oldest-pending dates frozen at 2026-08-23 / 08-23 / 08-20 / 08-26 / 08-27 / 08-28 while newest is 2026-09-05 00:55 — i.e. new rows are minted every tick and the head of the queue is never served. The four SMS sweeps that got the constant key show no such backlog.
findings.impact: Directly produces the lead's never-draining backlog and the Sentry KITABUYETU-1 starvation alerts. job_queue is 82,609 rows / 35 MB and job_logs 122,277 rows / 58 MB — together 93 MB of a 137 MB public schema, against 9 groups. Every tick's `SELECT type, MAX(priority) FROM job_queue WHERE status=$1 AND run_at<=NOW() GROUP BY type` (banked at 902 ms mean) scans a backlog that exists only because of this key.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same constant-dedup-key change to email_campaign_process, email_campaign_drain, email_retry_failed, mpesa_reconcile, mpesa_replay_callbacks and outbox_dispatch (all six are self-idempotent claim-what-is-due sweeps, same shape as the four already fixed), then purge the 19,463 stale pending rows.

findings.title: 12,025 job executions and 4.79 million ms of compute spent draining email campaign tables that have never held a single row
findings.evidence:
`SELECT q.type, l.message, count(*), sum(l.duration_ms) FROM job_logs l JOIN job_queue q ON q.id=l.job_id GROUP BY 1,2` → email_campaign_drain logs the literal message "Email campaign drain (0 sent, 0 failed of 0)" 5,992 times, 2,391,398 ms total, 399 ms mean; email_campaign_process logs "Email campaigns processed" 6,033 times, 2,379,464 ms, 394 ms mean. The "of 0" in every one of 5,992 runs is the proof the source set has always been empty.
Backing tables confirm it: exact counts via query_to_xml over pg_class show email_campaigns = 0 rows, email_campaign_recipients = 0 rows, email_templates = 0, email_schedules = 0. A further 3,702 + 3,652 = 7,354 copies of these two types sit pending and will each do the same nothing.
Same pattern, smaller: journal_lines_partition_maintenance logs "journal_lines partitions ensured through 3 months ahead (0 checked)" on all 8 of its runs (2026-09-01 06:00–06:55 UTC — 8 rows for a job scheduled once a month, so its dedup key is not holding either).
findings.impact: 4.77 million ms ≈ 1.33 hours of Vercel function time already spent producing nothing, plus 7,354 queued repeats. These two types also occupy tick budget ahead of email_retry_failed, which is why that job is cut off mid-run every tick (see the retry-loop finding).
findings.recommendation: Gate both enqueues on `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM email_campaigns WHERE status IN ('scheduled','sending'))` — or drop the campaign job types entirely until the campaign feature is launched. Delete the 7,354 pending rows.

findings.title: journal_lines partitioning: 328 lines of migration + service, a job type, a monthly schedule and a handler — all for a schema that exists only in CI
findings.evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260719000000_094_journal_lines_partitioned_table.sql (139 L) and 20260719010000_095_journal_lines_partition_swap.sql (62 L) are in the repo, applied by CI, and absent from production (pg_class relkind for public.journal_lines is 'r'; journal_lines_partitioned and journal_lines_legacy do not exist). Around them sits live machinery: lib/services/journal-lines-partitions.service.ts (127 L), the 'journal_lines_partition_maintenance' job type (lib/jobs/types.ts:21), its handler (lib/jobs/handlers.ts:86 and :454) and a monthly schedule (lib/jobs/index.ts:355-364). The service is self-aware — lib/services/journal-lines-partitions.service.ts:92-93 logs "journal_lines is not a partitioned table — migrations 094/095 are not applied. Skipping partition maintenance" — and production's job_logs confirms the no-op: 8 runs, all "(0 checked)".
The table being partitioned holds 66 rows (`SELECT count(*) FROM journal_lines`), against 12 journal_entries.
Four service files also carry comments that assert the partitioning is live and shape their SQL around it: lib/services/accounting.service.ts:106-108, :195, :301, lib/services/mpesa-charges.service.ts:105-108, lib/services/organization-finance.service.ts:423-426 ("entry_date is the journal_lines partition key — supplied directly").
findings.impact: 328 lines of dead code plus five misleading comments that will make the next reader believe partitioning is in force. More importantly it is the concrete cause of the CI/production schema divergence: the accounting integration suite runs against a partitioned journal_lines that production does not have.
findings.recommendation: Delete migrations 094/095, lib/services/journal-lines-partitions.service.ts, the job type, its handler branch and its schedule entry, and correct the five comments. A 66-row table on a 9-group system is nowhere near needing partitions; revisit if journal_lines ever exceeds a few hundred thousand rows.

findings.title: 11 database tables have zero rows AND zero references anywhere in the TypeScript source; 58 zero-row tables carry 295 indexes and 108 RLS policies
findings.evidence:
Exact counts (query_to_xml count(*) over every public relkind='r') give 58 zero-row tables of 144. Cross-referencing every table name against all tracked .ts/.tsx (excluding generated types/db.types.ts and __tests__) yields 11 with no production reference at all: contact_submissions, email_delivery_reports, email_failures, email_suppressions, idempotency_keys, invoice_line_items, newsletter_subscribers, notification_rules, platform_billing, platform_notifications, welfare_votes. Falsified further with loose greps ("suppress", "newsletter", "idempotenc", "welfare_vote", …) — the only hit is __tests__/integration/app-tenant/rls-policy-consolidation.test.ts:139-150, which is the sole writer of idempotency_keys.
Also checked from the DB side so DB-only consumers are not misjudged: `SELECT ... FROM pg_proc WHERE prosrc ILIKE '%<table>%'` returns 0 for all 11 (invoice_sequences and share_certificate_counters DO have a referencing function, so they were excluded from the list). Control run against 12 known-live tables (loans 81 refs, contributions 91, members 232, sms_credit_ledger 1, staff_alert_state 2, sms_provider_health_state 1) — every one returns ≥1, so a 0 is meaningful.
Aggregate cost: `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE n=0), sum(pg_total_relation_size) FILTER (WHERE n=0), indexes, policies, triggers` → 58 tables, 2,932,736 bytes, 295 of the schema's 800 indexes, 108 of its 276 RLS policies, 28 triggers.
Note the duplication: idempotency_keys duplicates a concern already implemented in Redis at lib/utils/idempotency.ts:20 — the Postgres table is the abandoned half.
findings.impact: Storage is trivial (2.8 MB), but 108 RLS policies and 295 indexes on empty tables are real maintenance surface — this repo has twice re-opened a PostgREST hole through grant/rename churn, and every policy on a table nobody uses is another chance to do it again. It also inflates the 481 idx_scan=0 indexes the lead measured: 295 of them sit on tables that have never held a row.
findings.recommendation: Drop the 11 fully orphaned tables (with their policies, indexes and triggers) in one migration. Keep the other 47 zero-row tables but treat them as unlaunched-feature surface, not schema debt. Delete idempotency_keys specifically — Redis already owns that concern and having two implementations invites someone to wire the wrong one.

findings.title: /api/v1/mpesa/c2b is a live, authentication-exempt duplicate of the daraja C2B pair that nothing can ever legitimately call
findings.evidence:
app/api/v1/mpesa/c2b/route.ts (124 L) imports handleC2BConfirmation and validateC2BAccount from lib/services/mpesa.service and runs the full confirmation path (route line 64: `await handleC2BConfirmation(body, callerIp)`), which is the exact same handler app/api/v1/daraja/c2b-confirm/route.ts:35 calls.
It cannot be reached legitimately: registerC2BUrls (lib/services/daraja.service.ts:372-386) registers ConfirmationURL=`${CALLBACK_BASE}/api/v1/daraja/c2b-confirm` and ValidationURL=`${CALLBACK_BASE}/api/v1/daraja/c2b-validate` — never /api/v1/mpesa/c2b — and registerC2BUrls itself has zero call sites. Scanning all 1,166 tracked files for a quoted reference to the path finds none; the only textual hits (`/mpesa/c2b/${version}/registerurl` at daraja.service.ts:378 and `[mpesa/c2b]` logger prefixes) are Safaricom's own API path and log tags.
It is nonetheless exempt from auth: proxy.ts:146 `pathname.startsWith('/api/v1/mpesa/c2b')` sits in the no-token allowlist alongside the real callbacks, and the route performs no Safaricom IP check (assertSafaricomIp, daraja.service.ts:203, is not called).
findings.impact: 124 lines of duplicate code, and worse: an unauthenticated, unregistered, publicly-routable endpoint that hands attacker-supplied JSON to the money-routing handler. Dead code that is still routable is strictly worse than dead code that is not.
findings.recommendation: Delete app/api/v1/mpesa/c2b/route.ts and remove proxy.ts:146 from the auth-exempt list. Separately (not a deletion): registerC2BUrls has zero call sites, so the daraja URLs are only registered because someone did it by hand — wire it into a deploy step or an admin action so the registration is reproducible.

findings.title: 11 API routes (~644 lines) have no caller anywhere in the repo and no external registration
findings.evidence:
Scanned all 239 app/api/**/route.ts against every tracked .ts/.tsx/.js file for a quoted occurrence of the route path, testing both the full path and the prefix-stripped form the client uses (lib/api/client.ts:5-6 sets BASE='/api/v1', ADMIN_BASE='/api/admin', so endpoints.ts writes '/auth/login' not '/api/v1/auth/login'). Excluded non-caller reference sites (robots.ts, lib/auth/subscription-gate.ts, proxy.ts, __tests__). Controls pass: /api/admin/groups, /api/admin/dashboard, /api/v1/members, /api/v1/welfare all resolve to real callers.
28 routes had no caller; 17 are legitimately external and were cleared by direct evidence — /api/cron (`SELECT jobname, schedule, command FROM cron.job` → one active job, every 5 min, POSTing https://kitabuyetu.vercel.app/api/cron), /api/v1/mpesa/callback (registered as CallBackURL at daraja.service.ts:311), /api/v1/daraja/c2b-{confirm,validate}, the QStash workers, /api/health*. The remaining 11 have neither a caller nor a registration:
  app/api/admin/governance/compute/route.ts (27 L) — zero textual hits repo-wide
  app/api/admin/policies/route.ts (31 L), /loan (27 L), /loan-terms (27 L), /posting-templates (28 L) — zero hits; endpoints.ts:584 exposes only '/organization/policies', a different route
  app/api/v1/mpesa/qr/route.ts (76 L) — closed dead loop: its only service, generateDynamicQr (daraja.service.ts:913), is imported by this route alone; mpesa_qr_codes has 0 rows
  app/api/v1/mpesa/transaction-status/route.ts (96 L) — same closed loop with queryTransactionStatus (daraja.service.ts:665)
  app/api/v1/mpesa/stk-query/route.ts (70 L)
  app/api/v1/settings/contribution-splits/[id]/route.ts (42 L) — the page (app/(dashboard)/settings/contribution-splits/page.tsx:47,88) only GETs and PUTs the collection
  app/api/v1/welfare/pool/route.ts (29 L)
  app/api/v1/email/webhooks/sendgrid/route.ts (67 L) — `SELECT provider, count(*) FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1` returns only resend and smtp, so SendGrid has never been the provider
Four more route families are reachable only from integration tests: /api/v1/mpesa/bill-manager (259 L, bill_manager_invoices = 0 rows), /api/v1/mpesa/disbursements + [id] (69 L), /api/v1/payment-requests + [id] (79 L), /api/v1/welfare/[id] (33 L).
findings.impact: ~644 lines of routes that ship in every build and every deployment, each carrying its own auth wiring, validators and entitlement-map entries that must stay correct through refactors. Four of them (the admin policy quartet) are super_admin-gated write endpoints with no UI, so platform-wide loan terms and posting templates can only be changed by hand-crafting a request.
findings.recommendation: Delete the 11 unreachable routes, or — for the admin policy quartet and governance/compute, which look like intended admin capability — wire the missing UI. Decide the test-only routes deliberately: /api/v1/mpesa/bill-manager is 259 lines plus six Daraja functions for a feature with zero rows.

findings.title: 512 lines of email service functions are never called, and 3 of the 5 provider adapters (303 lines) have never been selected in production
findings.evidence:
Extracted all 779 exported value identifiers under lib/ and searched every other tracked .ts/.tsx for each; 80 are referenced nowhere outside their own file and 34 more only from __tests__. The email cluster dominates:
  lib/services/notification-email.service.ts — 7 of 8 exports dead: sendContributionReminder(:56), sendLoanApprovedEmail(:86), sendLoanRejectedEmail(:114), sendLoanDisbursedEmail(:140), sendLoanRepaymentReceivedEmail(:170), sendMeetingInvites(:200), sendMeetingReminders(:233) — ~205 of 260 lines. Only sendContributionConfirmation is used (by contributions.service.ts).
  lib/services/member-email.service.ts — sendWelcomeEmail(:5), sendOtpEmail(:29), sendAccountUpdateEmail(:53), sendMonthlyStatements(:101) all uncalled (~105 of 151 lines).
  lib/services/report-email.service.ts — emailPnlReport(:7), emailBalanceSheet(:27), broadcastFinancialReport(:48) uncalled (~77 of 159).
  lib/services/billing-email.service.ts — sendInvoiceEmail(:84), sendReceiptEmail(:240) uncalled (~125 of 395).
  lib/email/provider.ts:51 — sendEmail() exported and never imported; every caller uses sendEmailWithFallback.
Adapters: lib/email/provider.ts:14-23 selects one adapter from EMAIL_PROVIDER. `SELECT provider, count(*), min(created_at)::date, max(created_at)::date FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1` returns exactly two rows — resend (24,383, since 2026-06-02) and smtp (23,550, since 2026-08-16). sendgrid.ts (109 L), ses.ts (92 L) and mailgun.ts (105 L) have never produced a row.
Side effect worth noting: PR #148's fix to the loan_approved email edits lib/email/templates/defaults.ts:100, a template reachable only through sendLoanApprovedEmail — i.e. dead code.
findings.impact: ~815 lines carried through every build and typecheck. Each adapter independently reimplements the same email_logs INSERT/UPDATE trio (resend.ts:21/67/80, smtp.ts:30/74/87, sendgrid.ts:17/88/100, ses.ts:29/71/83, mailgun.ts:24/84/96) — five copies of one concern, so any schema change to email_logs must be made five times.
findings.recommendation: Delete the three unused adapters and the sendgrid webhook route; if multi-provider support is wanted later, restore from git rather than carrying it. Delete the uncalled email functions, or wire them — several (loan approved/disbursed, meeting invites, welcome, OTP) look like intended product behaviour that silently does not exist. Hoist the shared email_logs INSERT/UPDATE out of the remaining adapters into one place.

findings.title: The SMTP fallback has attempted 23,556 sends since 2026-08-16 and delivered zero, paying a connection timeout on every primary-provider failure
findings.evidence:
lib/email/provider.ts:70-74 — when the primary adapter fails and SMTP_HOST is set, every send retries through `new SmtpAdapter().send(payload)`. `SELECT provider, status, count(*) FROM email_logs GROUP BY 1,2` → smtp: 19,686 failed, 3,870 queued, **0 sent**, ever. The failure text is visible in the retry stream: `SELECT created_at, status, error_message FROM email_logs WHERE template_key='group_verification_link' ORDER BY created_at DESC` shows the pair "You have reached your daily email sending quota" (resend) followed ~0.6 s later by "Greeting never received" (smtp) on every single tick.
A further 3,870 smtp rows are stuck in status='queued' — never marked failed, so retryFailedEmails() (which filters on status='failed') will never even see them; they are pure orphan rows.
findings.impact: Every failed email pays an SMTP connect-and-timeout on top of the primary failure, and doubles the email_logs write rate (2 rows per send attempt instead of 1) — roughly half of the 22 MB table. The fallback offers zero availability benefit because it has never once worked.
findings.recommendation: Either fix the SMTP credentials/host or unset SMTP_HOST so lib/email/provider.ts:71 stops taking the branch. Also make the adapter mark its own failures as 'failed' rather than leaving rows at 'queued', so orphans do not accumulate invisibly.

findings.title: The invoicing subsystem has never produced an invoice, yet two scheduled jobs and 395 lines of service run against it
findings.evidence: Exact counts: invoices = 0, invoice_items = 0, invoice_line_items = 0, invoice_schedules = 0, invoice_sequences = 0 — the sequence table has never even been incremented, so no invoice number has ever been minted. invoice_line_items additionally has zero code references anywhere (see the orphan-tables finding). Meanwhile `SELECT q.type, count(*), sum(l.duration_ms) FROM job_logs l JOIN job_queue q ON q.id=l.job_id GROUP BY 1` shows email_overdue_invoices 178 runs / 79,002 ms and email_recurring_invoices 89 runs / 39,535 ms, both driven from lib/services/billing-email.service.ts (395 L, of which sendInvoiceEmail and sendReceiptEmail are entirely uncalled).
findings.impact: 267 scheduled executions and ~119 s of compute producing nothing, plus 5 tables with their indexes and policies. Small in absolute terms, but it is another unconditional timer whose queue rows compete for the same tick budget that is starving email_retry_failed.
findings.recommendation: Gate both job enqueues on the existence of an open invoice, and treat invoicing as unlaunched rather than live. Drop invoice_line_items (orphaned in both code and data — invoice_items is the one the code actually uses).

findings.title: WhatsApp has never delivered a message: all 317 rows are outbound dry-runs, and its 259-line webhook has never received anything
findings.evidence: `SELECT count(*), string_agg(DISTINCT direction||':'||status, ', '), max(created_at) FROM whatsapp_messages` → 317 rows, the ONLY distinct value is `outbound:dry_run`, most recent 2026-09-03 14:14. Zero inbound rows means app/api/v1/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts (259 L) has never received a real delivery. lib/integrations/whatsapp-client.ts:58 explains the state: it returns `{status:'dry_run', reason:'WhatsApp credentials not configured (set WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID + WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN)'}`. Subsystem size: whatsapp.service.ts (222 L) + whatsapp-client.ts (110 L) + webhook route (259 L) + 3 API routes (57 L) = 648 L, plus a 320 kB table with 7 indexes. The UI at app/(dashboard)/whatsapp/page.tsx is live and calls it, so users are composing messages that are silently discarded.
findings.impact: 648 lines and a table maintained for a channel that has never sent anything. The user-facing half is worse than dead: the dashboard accepts and records messages that go nowhere, with 'dry_run' the only signal.
findings.recommendation: Either configure WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID/WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, or hide the WhatsApp dashboard page behind whatsappService.isConfigured() (already exposed at app/api/v1/whatsapp/status/route.ts:13) so nobody composes into a void. Do not delete the subsystem without a product decision.

findings.title: 7 source files (362 lines) have no importer anywhere, and one of them is the sole consumer of an npm dependency
findings.evidence:
Resolved every module under lib/, components/, hooks/, emails/, providers/ against all tracked files by import specifier, then confirmed each candidate with a direct name grep across the repo (excluding the file's own definition). Zero importers, including tests:
  components/marketing/role-cards.tsx (94 L)
  components/marketing/resources-section.tsx (61 L)
  components/marketing/impact-section.tsx (51 L)
  components/marketing/why-kitabu-yetu-section.tsx (38 L)

findings.title: Six M-Pesa capabilities are fully built and wired but have never executed once in production
findings.evidence: Every backing table is empty (exact counts): mpesa_b2c_transactions = 0, mpesa_b2b_transactions = 0, mpesa_reversals = 0, mpesa_charges = 0, mpesa_qr_codes = 0, bill_manager_invoices = 0 — against mpesa_stk_requests = 46, mpesa_callbacks = 81, mpesa_transactions = 57 for the paths that are live. The settlement/vendor stack that sits on B2B/B2C is likewise empty: settlement_requests = 0, settlement_approvals = 0, vendor_payments = 0, group_bank_accounts = 0. Code footprint: b2b route 155 L + service 43 L; b2c route 130 L + service 368 L; reversal route 127 L; airtime route 76 L + service 113 L (isAirtimeConfigured, daraja.service.ts:516, has zero callers); bill-manager route 259 L + six Daraja functions (daraja.service.ts:752-863); qr route 76 L; transaction-status route 96 L — plus settlements.service.ts 294 L, vendor-payments.service.ts 320 L, settlement-approvals.service.ts 59 L, group-bank-accounts.service.ts 145 L. Two of these are closed dead loops with no caller at all (qr, transaction-status — see the unreachable-routes finding). The same pattern holds outside M-Pesa: shares (share_classes/share_holdings/share_transactions/share_certificate_counters all 0) costs routes 235 L + service 792 L + page 734 L, and dividends (both tables 0) costs 192 L + 728 L + 777 L.
findings.impact: Roughly 5,500 lines of built-but-never-run code, and it is the main driver of the 58 zero-row tables carrying 295 indexes and 108 RLS policies. This is product backlog rather than waste — but it is why a 9-group, 4-loan system has a 144-table schema, and every one of those RLS policies is surface that renames and grant changes can silently break.
findings.recommendation: Do not delete — this is deliberate unlaunched capability (settlements/B2C were rebuilt as recently as 2026-08-11). Do register the debt explicitly: keep a list of the unlaunched subsystems so schema-wide changes (renames, grant sweeps, RLS consolidations) can be reviewed against them, and resist adding indexes to zero-row tables until a feature actually ships.

findings.title: 80 exported lib/ identifiers are referenced nowhere outside their own file; 34 more only from tests
findings.evidence: Extracted all `export (async )?(function|const|class) <name>` declarations under lib/ (779 identifiers) and word-searched every other tracked .ts/.tsx. 80 have zero external references and 34 are referenced only from __tests__. Beyond the email cluster reported separately: lib/services/daraja.service.ts exports DEFAULT_SAFARICOM_IPS, getMpesaTimestamp, getMpesaPassword, isAirtimeConfigured and reconcileBillManagerPayment with no consumers; lib/services/mpesa-allocation.service.ts exports applyPartialRepayment, applyLoanWaterfall and insertSavingsContribution unused; lib/redis/index.ts exports getRefreshToken and getLoginAttempts unused; lib/supabase/server.ts exports createAdminClient unused; lib/services/sms-analytics.service.ts exports smsAnalyticsService and lib/services/sms-pricing.service.ts exports smsPricingService, neither named anywhere else. Nine validator modules export constant arrays (CAPITAL_MODELS, LOSS_BEARERS, DIVIDEND_STATUSES, WHATSAPP_STATUSES, RELIABILITY_TIERS, SHARE_TXN_TYPES, ANALYTICS_PERIODS, PERIODS_PER_YEAR, TARGETABLE_ROLES) that nothing imports. Test-only exports include lib/db/index.ts:tenantPool, lib/auth/jwt.ts:verifyAccessToken and lib/utils/currency.ts's four decimal helpers.
findings.impact: Not bytes — visibility. An exported symbol reads as public API, so each of these is a false signal that something depends on it, which makes refactoring the surrounding module more cautious than it needs to be. Several (applyLoanWaterfall, insertSavingsContribution, reconcileBillManagerPayment) sit on money paths and look load-bearing while being unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Downgrade to module-private (drop `export`) anything used only inside its own file, and delete the ones used nowhere. Where a test is the only consumer (verifyAccessToken, tenantPool, the currency helpers), keep the export but mark it as test-surface so nobody assumes production depends on it.
